commit_message:
[DispatchCreation] Collapse named contractions with user indexing maps (#25113)

A linalg.batch_matmul whose RHS indexing map drops the batch dim (the
usual `x @ W` with a leading batch) was never collapsed:
CollapseDimensions only considered linalg.generic, and
AnnotateDataTilingHints rejects the resulting two-M-dim contraction. The
same op written as a generic collapsed to a 2-D matmul and was
data-tiled, so data tiling depended on the named vs. generic form, and
on O2, where generalize-matmul hides the difference.

Make named contractions with projected-permutation maps eligible for
collapsing, in dispatch regions and in the standalone contraction
collapse pass, and generalize them before collapsing: upstream's
named-op collapse path clones the op with collapsed operands, which is
only valid when the collapse keeps the op's structure (e.g.
linalg.fill). Named contractions with their default maps have no
collapsible loops and are unaffected, and ones carrying a
compilation_info or lowering_config keep their loop space, as that
configuration refers to the original loops.

Fixes #25110.

Signed-off-by: Florian Walbroel <walbroel@roofline.ai>
Co-authored-by: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

[Codegen][CPU] Cover the #24932 benchmark matrix in inner_tiled lit tests

Pin the cost model's distribution picks for the #24932 shapes (64^3,
256^3, 81x41x19, 540x516x332) with packed operands from real compiles.
The RVV file sweeps --iree-llvmcpu-number-of-threads=8/4/1 (small shapes
consolidate tiles as threads drop; large stays [18,1,0]; dynamic falls
back to [1,1,0]); the x86 file covers the same matrix at 8 threads.

commit_message:
[DispatchCreation] Collapse named contractions with user indexing maps (#25113)

A linalg.batch_matmul whose RHS indexing map drops the batch dim (the
usual `x @ W` with a leading batch) was never collapsed:
CollapseDimensions only considered linalg.generic, and
AnnotateDataTilingHints rejects the resulting two-M-dim contraction. The
same op written as a generic collapsed to a 2-D matmul and was
data-tiled, so data tiling depended on the named vs. generic form, and
on O2, where generalize-matmul hides the difference.

Make named contractions with projected-permutation maps eligible for
collapsing, in dispatch regions and in the standalone contraction
collapse pass, and generalize them before collapsing: upstream's
named-op collapse path clones the op with collapsed operands, which is
only valid when the collapse keeps the op's structure (e.g.
linalg.fill). Named contractions with their default maps have no
collapsible loops and are unaffected, and ones carrying a
compilation_info or lowering_config keep their loop space, as that
configuration refers to the original loops.

Fixes #25110.

Co-authored-by: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit_message:
[Build][AMDGPU] Use bitcode from the official ROCM distribution (#25133)

With the sunset of the old artifacts from
`shark-infra/amdgpu-device-libs`, migrate to LLVM bitcode blobs from the
official distribution. The version shall be pinned in
`build_tools/third_party/amdgpu_device_libs/rocm_package.json`.

This increases the bitcode download to 146Mb (in comparison, the WASI
SDK weighs in at <120Mb). Considering we're only using less than 1Mb,
that's unfortunate, but at the moment it's the only way to use the
official maintained source.

Fixes #25131.

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Write embedded executable object data before linking

Executable objects that carry inline data got a temporary file path,
but the data was never written to it.

The linker then received an empty object file.

Serialize the object data into the temporary file, then flush and close
the file so that the linker reads its complete contents.

Report an error if the temporary file cannot be created or the data
cannot be serialized.

Add a lit test in which a dispatch calls a function that only an inline
object defines, so the embedded linker reports an undefined symbol when
the object file is empty.

Assisted-by: Claude Opus 5.5

commit_message:
[DispatchCreation] Collapse named contractions with user indexing maps (#25113)

A linalg.batch_matmul whose RHS indexing map drops the batch dim (the
usual `x @ W` with a leading batch) was never collapsed:
CollapseDimensions only considered linalg.generic, and
AnnotateDataTilingHints rejects the resulting two-M-dim contraction. The
same op written as a generic collapsed to a 2-D matmul and was
data-tiled, so data tiling depended on the named vs. generic form, and
on O2, where generalize-matmul hides the difference.

Make named contractions with projected-permutation maps eligible for
collapsing, in dispatch regions and in the standalone contraction
collapse pass, and generalize them before collapsing: upstream's
named-op collapse path clones the op with collapsed operands, which is
only valid when the collapse keeps the op's structure (e.g.
linalg.fill). Named contractions with their default maps have no
collapsible loops and are unaffected, and ones carrying a
compilation_info or lowering_config keep their loop space, as that
configuration refers to the original loops.

Fixes #25110.

Signed-off-by: Florian Walbroel <walbroel@roofline.ai>
Co-authored-by: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
